questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: The narrator's drive to reach Hampton Institute and lessons learned on the way
The narrator's escape from slavery and his flight to Virginia
The narrator's work in the salt furnace and his early wages
The narrator's life as a teacher at a small coloured school
questions.explain: He hears of Hampton in the coal-mine, works for Mrs. Ruffner and sets out to go.

questions.q: How did the narrator first learn about Hampton Institute?
options: From a letter sent by a former classmate
By overhearing two miners talking in the coal-mine
From his teacher at the little coloured school
From Mrs. Ruffner, who had visited Hampton
questions.explain: He crept close to two miners discussing the school in the dark of the mine.

questions.q: How did he travel the remainder of the distance to Hampton after trains stopped?
options: A through train carried him the entire way
He walked for most of the remaining trip
He went the rest of the way by stage-coach
He continued by riverboat along the route
questions.explain: Trains ran only part of the way, and the remainder of the distance was travelled by stage-coaches.

questions.q: What did he use as his first library?
options: A wooden shelf built into the wall of the little school
A trunk of borrowed books kept under his mother's bed
A crate at the mine, filled with books from the miners
A dry-goods box with one side knocked out and shelves added
questions.explain: He turned a dry-goods box into a library of every book he could get.

questions.q: How did the narrator come to view Mrs. Ruffner?
options: As too strict to endure, so he left within a few weeks
As an obstacle who kept him from studying at night
As a friend, whose habits and lessons were as valuable as schooling
As a stranger who never trusted him with her household
questions.explain: He went from fearing her to seeing her as a best friend, valuing her lessons as much as any schooling.
